title: Computational Complexity of Approximate Fixed Points

problemStatement.formal: ∀ f : [0,1] → [0,1], Continuous f → ∃ x, f(x) = x. Complexity: O(log 1/ε) in 1D, PPAD-complete in ≥2D.
problemStatement.plain: What is the computational complexity of finding approximate Brouwer fixed points? Answer: O(log 1/ε) in 1D via binary search; PPAD-complete in ≥2D (Chen-Deng 2009).
whyMatters: Fundamental question in computational topology and algorithmic game theory
PPAD structure connects to Nash equilibrium computation

proven: 1D Discrete IVT (sign-changing sequence has adjacent sign change)
Approximate fixed points exist (from exact via IVT)
Approximate fixed points converge to exact ones
Binary search narrows sign-change intervals (1/2^n width)
